title: No. 4 UCLA survives Illinois, ties school record with 10th victory
content:
No. 4 UCLA tied a school record with its 10th win by defeating Illinois 22-14 on Friday night at the Rose Bowl in Pasadena, Calif., on Friday night.

The Bruins (10-0, 7-0 Big Ten) are one victory from clinching a spot in the 16th and final Big Ten title game on Dec. 5, which would be their first league championship appearance since 2012. Under first-year coach Bob Chesney, UCLA has completed one of the great turnarounds in college football history after a 3-9 finish last season.

“Resolve is the word I keep thinking about,” Chesney told Fox Sports after the game. “Relentlessness and resolve. We’re never going to give up. We’re never going to waver. It doesn’t matter who’s playing what position. We believe in everybody on this team. I mean, there’s a lot of things we got to clean up, but I’m ultimately really, really proud of the way they fought.”

The game wasn’t without drama, however. UCLA quarterback Ty Dieffenbach left with an upper-body injury late in the first half, forcing the Bruins to briefly turn to third-team quarterback Madden Iamaleava. In the driving rain, the Illini cut into UCLA’s lead, and the Bruins stalled on three consecutive drives.

With a standing ovation greeting him, Dieffenbach returned to the UCLA sideline and then the field late in the third quarter. He took the Bruins on a 75-yard drive, culminating in a touchdown pass to Semaj Morgan and a 19-7 lead.

Illinois (6-4, 4-3 Big Ten) battled back with a scoring drive of its own and had a chance to take the lead trailing by 5 points late in the game. But UCLA’s Scooter Jackson picked off a pass by Katin Houser, leading to a Bruins field goal and the final margin.

Dieffenbach, a transfer from Cal Poly, has started four consecutive games after replacing original starter Nico Iamaleava, who suffered a torn ACL in a win against Oregon. Dieffenbach finished with 232 passing yards and two touchdowns.

This year’s Bruins also have tied the school record for wins to start the season, which it set in 1998. That’s also the last time they won a conference title.

Nearly as important as the victory was the manner in which it happened. In the last two weeks, UCLA has faced physical and traditional Big Ten programs without backing down. Illinois had won four straight Big Ten games, including a 21-10 victory against Oregon.

The Bruins wrap up the season against two traditional heavyweights. Next week, they play at Michigan before closing the season at home against crosstown rival USC.
